summary: A square weather symbol drawn with circles, rounded rectangles, lines and a crescent path: sun, cloud, rain, snow, storm, partly cloudy or fog, with a moon instead of the sun at night. Opt-in morph mode: one outline that morphs smoothly between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm when a value changes, with optional animated rays, rain, snow and lightning.

condition.doc: Codes, in order: sun: an amber disc with eight rays; cloud: a grey cloud; rain: a cloud over three slanted blue drops; snow: a cloud over three blue flakes (dots); storm: a cloud over an amber lightning bolt; partly: partly cloudy, a small sun (a crescent moon at night) behind a grey cloud; fog: a cloud over two horizontal grey lines. Static: to switch it at run time, put one call per condition in a stateLayout driven by a host integer. Ignored when morph is true

night.doc: Night: a crescent moon replaces the sun in sun (clear) and partly. A number or a "@variable" (0 day, 1 night), read at run time, so a host flag such as "@isNight" switches it while the document plays; omitted or 0 draws the day icon only. Other conditions ignore it

size.doc: Width and height in dp; the drawing is on a 24-unit grid scaled to it (and down to a smaller box)

label.doc: Accessibility label, a text or a "@textVariable"; by default Sunny, Cloudy, Rain, Snow, Thunderstorm, Partly cloudy or Fog (with night given: Clear for sun, since the same label must hold by day and by night; pass a label such as "Clear night" for a fixed night icon)

morph.doc: Opt-in morph mode: one outline that morphs smoothly between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm whenever value changes (a host variable, a tap), instead of the fixed condition drawing. 'partly', 'fog' and night are not part of it

value.doc: With morph: the condition as a number or "@variable": 0 sun, 1 cloud, 2 rain, 3 snow, 4 storm. A change eases the old outline into the new one over duration seconds (any pair: sun straight to storm does not pass through the others)

duration.doc: With morph: the morph's length in seconds (the standard cubic easing). Mono has no motion: the drawing switches

animate.doc: With morph: the details move: the sun's rays turn and pulse, rain falls, snow drifts, the bolt flickers and the icon floats. It repaints every frame while shown; off (the default), they hold still. Always still in mono

look.doc: With morph: flat fills the outline with the colour params (theme colours by default, for icons on a surface); rich is an illustration for coloured skies: gradient bodies (amber sun, white clouds, slate rain cloud, dark storm), a glow behind the sun and a faint edge. Mono ignores it

sunColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the sun disc and rays (flat look only)

cloudColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the cloud, rain and snow clouds (flat look only)

stormColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the storm cloud (flat look only)

dropColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the rain

flakeColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the snow

boltColor.doc: With morph: the colour of the bolt

pitfalls: condition is static: each condition is a different drawing written into the document. To show a condition the host chooses at run time, put one call per condition in a stateLayout (or behind visibility) driven by a host number: a float variable, which stateLayout reads as its index and a TextChoice for the condition word can read too (a TextChoice reads an integer variable as 0). night, by contrast, is read at run time: with a "@variable" both the sun and the moon are written, each in a conditionalOperations block (night < 0.5 draws the sun, >= 0.5 the moon)
No SVG paths: the cloud is three circles over a rounded rectangle, and the bolt three round-capped lines (an SVG path string costs about 4 KB in Java, padded to 1024 floats)

The moon is a crescent path (pathData from an op list of cubics, about 200 B), not an SVG string and not a disc with a background-coloured bite, so it sits on any surface; mono strokes the same path as an outline

Mono draws the cloud as an outline: the same shapes 1.25 units larger in onSurface, then the shapes themselves in @colors.background, so the ring follows their union. It assumes the icon sits on the background colour, which every surface is in mono
The sun's eight rays are one line drawn in a loop that rotates the canvas 45° per pass (8 × 45° = 360°, back to the start)
The drawing is scaled to the box the layout actually gives the canvas (min of its width and height, centred), so a call clamped by a smaller parent shrinks instead of being cut off
partly draws the small sun or moon first and the cloud over it: the filled cloud (or, in mono, its background-filled outline) hides the part behind it

Morph mode (morph: true) reads value (0 sun, 1 cloud, 2 rain, 3 snow, 4 storm) at run time: one call follows a host variable or a tap, no stateLayout needed. Each condition has an eased weight (anim of 1 - |value - i|) and four chained pathTweens give each outline its weight, so a change from a to b is a pure a-to-b morph. Fractions blend outlines (2.5 is half rain cloud, half snow cloud)

The five outlines are op-list paths from the weather-outline generator, written once per document (about 4.5 KB for the five, shared by every morph call); each morph call adds about 1.5 KB (flat) or 2 KB (rich) for the tweens and details. For a row of icons that never changes at run time, the static condition is much smaller

Morph mode names its variables wxw0..wxw4, wxt, wxp, wxq and wxf and its paths wxM1..wxM3 and wxBody: every call redefines them in its own canvas, so several calls coexist, but don't use those names in the document

animate repaints every frame while the icon is on screen (continuousSec); leave it off for widgets and lists. Mono is always still and has no morph motion (the expansion removes every anim): the outline switches

In morph mode size is still what the canvas asks for, and the drawing scales to the box it gets: to size it from an expression, put the call in a box whose width and height are that expression and give size a large value
